description: Ibuprofen can blunt the antiplatelet effect of low-dose aspirin and raises GI bleeding risk when combined.
Combined use markedly increases the risk of serious bleeding.
Alcohol increases the risk of lactic acidosis with metformin.
Azithromycin may potentiate warfarin's anticoagulant effect; monitor INR.
Regular high-dose paracetamol may modestly increase INR; usually clinically minor.
NSAIDs may reduce the antihypertensive effect of losartan.
NSAIDs may modestly reduce blood-pressure control with amlodipine.
NSAIDs may reduce telmisartan's antihypertensive effect.
Cetirizine can add to clonazepam's sedation and impair alertness.
Levocetirizine can enhance clonazepam-related drowsiness and psychomotor impairment.
Aluminium-containing antacids can reduce fexofenadine absorption; separate doses by several hours.
Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 and can reduce activation and antiplatelet effect of clopidogrel.
Rabeprazole has less CYP2C19 inhibition than omeprazole but may still modestly reduce clopidogrel activation.
Pantoprazole has relatively little CYP2C19 inhibition and is less likely to reduce clopidogrel activation.
Amlodipine can modestly increase atorvastatin exposure; monitor for statin adverse effects.
Rosuvastatin may increase INR in patients receiving warfarin; monitor INR after initiation or dose changes.
Atorvastatin may increase warfarin effect; monitor INR after starting or changing statin therapy.
Amlodipine increases simvastatin exposure; simvastatin dosing should be limited.
Fluconazole can increase glimepiride exposure and cause prolonged hypoglycemia.
Ciprofloxacin can alter glucose control and has been associated with hypoglycemia in sulfonylurea users.
Combining sitagliptin with insulin increases hypoglycemia risk.
Iodinated contrast can increase the risk of metformin-associated lactic acidosis in susceptible patients.
Prednisolone can raise blood glucose and increase insulin requirements.
Prednisolone can reduce glucose control and counteract glimepiride's glucose-lowering effect.
NSAIDs may reduce telmisartan's antihypertensive effect and impair renal function.
Naproxen may reduce losartan's blood-pressure effect and increase renal impairment risk.
Concurrent use may increase dizziness or hypotension in susceptible patients.
Atenolol can mask adrenergic symptoms of hypoglycemia and may prolong hypoglycemia.
Atenolol can antagonize salbutamol's bronchodilator effect and may cause bronchospasm in susceptible patients.
Amlodipine may increase digoxin concentrations in some patients; monitor digoxin effects and levels.
Clarithromycin can markedly increase digoxin exposure and toxicity risk.
Amiodarone substantially increases digoxin concentrations and toxicity risk; dose reduction and monitoring are often required.
Verapamil can increase digoxin concentrations and slow cardiac conduction, increasing toxicity risk.
Ibuprofen can reduce renal lithium clearance and increase lithium concentrations.
Naproxen can reduce renal lithium clearance and increase lithium concentrations.
Diclofenac can reduce renal lithium clearance and increase lithium concentrations.
Telmisartan may reduce lithium clearance and increase lithium concentrations to potentially toxic levels.
Losartan may reduce lithium clearance and increase lithium concentrations to potentially toxic levels.
Thiazide diuretics substantially reduce lithium clearance and can cause lithium toxicity.
Combined use can increase sedation and psychomotor impairment.
Combined use increases gastrointestinal bleeding risk compared with either drug alone.
Escitalopram can increase bleeding risk when combined with warfarin.
Fluconazole inhibits warfarin metabolism and can markedly increase INR and bleeding risk.
Fluconazole can increase atorvastatin exposure and the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis.
Itraconazole strongly inhibits CYP3A4 and can markedly increase atorvastatin exposure and myopathy risk.
Itraconazole markedly increases simvastatin exposure and can cause severe myopathy or rhabdomyolysis.
Fluconazole can increase phenytoin concentrations and cause toxicity.
Fluconazole may increase clonazepam exposure and enhance sedation.
Phenytoin can unpredictably alter warfarin effect; close INR monitoring is required.
Valproate can increase free phenytoin concentrations and phenytoin toxicity risk.
Valproate markedly reduces lamotrigine clearance and increases serious skin-reaction risk.
Phenytoin can increase thyroid hormone metabolism and reduce levothyroxine effectiveness.
Calcium carbonate reduces levothyroxine absorption; separate administration by at least four hours.
Iron supplements reduce levothyroxine absorption; separate administration by at least four hours.
Long-term acid suppression may reduce levothyroxine absorption and increase thyroid-stimulating hormone in some patients.
Ciprofloxacin can increase warfarin effect and INR; monitor anticoagulation closely.
Levofloxacin can increase warfarin effect and INR; monitor anticoagulation closely.
Doxycycline can enhance warfarin anticoagulation and increase INR.
Amoxicillin may increase INR in some warfarin-treated patients; monitor during antibiotic therapy.
Clarithromycin increases atorvastatin exposure and the risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
Clarithromycin can increase warfarin exposure and anticoagulant effect, raising bleeding risk.
Aluminium or magnesium antacids reduce ciprofloxacin absorption; separate administration by several hours.
Aluminium or magnesium antacids reduce levofloxacin absorption; separate administration by several hours.
Calcium binds doxycycline and reduces its absorption; separate administration by several hours.
Iron binds doxycycline and substantially reduces its absorption; separate administration by several hours.
Concurrent use increases gastrointestinal irritation and bleeding risk.
Concurrent use increases gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding risk.
Ibuprofen increases bleeding risk when combined with apixaban.
Naproxen increases bleeding risk when combined with apixaban.
Ibuprofen increases gastrointestinal and overall bleeding risk with clopidogrel.
Naproxen increases gastrointestinal and overall bleeding risk with clopidogrel.
Ibuprofen increases gastrointestinal and systemic bleeding risk with warfarin.
Naproxen increases gastrointestinal and systemic bleeding risk with warfarin.
Cyclosporine markedly increases rosuvastatin exposure and the risk of myopathy.
Clarithromycin markedly increases simvastatin exposure and the risk of rhabdomyolysis.
